newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan says ban on Taiwan pork to have no impact.
newsitem.headline: Japan says ban on Taiwan pork to have no impact.

text.p: Japan's Agriculture Ministry said on Friday that it sees no immediate impact on domestic supplies from an import ban on Taiwanese pork, as Japan has ample stocks.

"We have imposed an import ban on Taiwanese pork for an indefinite period, following a notice from Taiwanese authorities," Akinori Aonuma, director of the Agriculture Ministry's animal health division, told reporters.
"But we don't expect any immediate impact on domestic supplies because of larger-than-usual stocks here," he said.

At the end of January, Japan had 172,000 tonnes of pork, including locally produced and imported meat, in storage, ministry data showed. Stock levels of between 80,000 and 90,000 tonnes are regarded as sufficient.

On Thursday, Taiwan banned all pork exports following an outbreak of the highly contagious foot and mouth disease in its hog population, spelling huge losses for one of the island's top export industries.

Taiwan's Council of Agriculture, which said laboratory results confirmed an outbreak of foot and mouth in nine counties and ordered the temporary export ban, warned that Taiwan faced a daunting task in eradicating the deadly disease.
"But in the longer term, Japanese importers are expected to shift to other supply sources such as the U.S. and Europe," the farm ministry's Aonuma said.
Japan had been importing some 16,000 tonnes of fresh and frozen pork from Taiwan per month, despite Tokyo's imposition of a special "emergency" tariff to limit imports and protect local breeders.
Another Agriculture Ministry official said that Japan has no plan to alter its special emergency import tariff on pork.
"We're going to keep the special pork tariff until this June as announced earlier. This has nothing to do with the import ban on Taiwanese pork," the official said.
